title: AI may help catch heart transplant rejection without biopsies
source_used: UA.News, relaying News-Medical; Medical Xpress page returned 403
key_facts: Researchers at NYU Langone Health tested an AI model that analyzes electrocardiograms (ECGs) and blood tests to detect heart transplant rejection.
Models were trained on 5,300 ECGs from 2,357 adult heart transplant recipients treated in 2018 to 2024, matched to biopsies from the previous month.
One model used ECG only; the other combined ECG with two blood tests (gene-activity markers and donor DNA fragments).
In a test group of 38 patients, the combined model correctly identified 94% of people with no rejection.
The blood-only approach wrongly flagged 19 patients as possibly needing a biopsy; the combined approach could spare them.
Published online 25 Sep 2026 in JHLT Open; authors call it the first to combine these biomarkers and ECG in one model compared directly to biopsy.
Next step is testing in more patients at several transplant centers.
quote_evidence: The next step will be to test the model in a larger number of patients at several transplant centers.
why_it_matters_hint: An AI model might let some transplant patients skip invasive heart biopsies, but it was tested on only 38 patients.
